To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the photoluminescent behavior of Be implanted Si doped GaAs is dominated by GaAs antisite defect formation and that this formation occurs at temperatures above 700°C.
the band-to-band peak in the Si dopped GaAs is smaller than reported values and that the luminescence from the implanted samples is attributed to GaAs antisite and vacancy defects.

the band-to-band peak energies in the unimplantd (reference) Si-doped GaA are smaller than reported values for the same carrier concentration in Te-doped material, and that the dominant luminescences for the Be implanted samples annealed at temperatures of 600°C or greater are associated with GaAs anti-site defects.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the photoluminescent response of Si-doped and Be-implanted GaAs as a function of carrier concentration and anneal temperature.
understanding the role of defects in the photoluminescent behavior of GaAs.
the photoluminescent properties of Be implanted, Si-doped GaAS after high temperature annealing.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the luminescence peak height is a function of the anneal temperature and the time, and the peak energy is dependent on the carrier and vacancy concentrations.
the photoluminesence of Si-doped n-type GaAS is dependent on the implantation damage and anneal conditions.

the photoluminescent properties of GaAs implanted with 1.2 MeV Be ions at room temperature and subsequently annealed at temperatures between 400°C and800°C for periods up to 30 min can be explained in terms of the creation of antisite defects.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the photoluminescent properties of Be implanted GaAs are very similar to those of Te implanted GaAs.
the photoluminescent properties of Be implanted Si doped n-type material are similar to that of Be implanted Te-doped n-type material.
the Be implantation process and the subsequent annealing at 800°C have a significant impact on the photoluminescent properties of Si-doped n-type GaAS.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the luminescence peak energy in Si-doped GaAS is smaller than reported values for Te doped GaAs of comparable carrier concentration.
the luminescence of implanted and annealed Si-doped GaAS can provide a means to probe defect formation and recovery.
the band-to-band peak position is smaller than previously reported values and the luminescence is dominated by antisite defects at high anneal temperatures.
